name: typify-property-presence
instr:
Please add an opt-in property-presence mode to typify so generated types can represent patch documents without losing the difference between an omitted field and a supplied value.

Expose `typify::TypeSpaceSettings::with_property_presence(&mut self, enabled: bool) -> &mut Self`. It defaults to false, and the last call wins. When enabled, every declared, non-required object property has an outer `Option<T>` for presence, where `T` is its normal schema-derived payload type, without the usual optional-field wrapping. `None` means omitted; `Some(value)` means supplied. For a nullable string this is `Option<Option<String>>`: `{}` is `None`, `{"label":null}` is `Some(None)`, and `{"label":"x"}` is `Some(Some("x"))`. Serialization and deserialization must retain that distinction and validate supplied values against the payload type.

In this mode, missing properties stay absent rather than taking their schema property defaults or intrinsic empty values. When deriving a nullable payload, keep a `null` default from being validated as a default of its non-null branch, since this can reject an otherwise valid schema before presence wrapping happens. A whole-type schema default instead retains exactly the declared keys supplied in that default. Builders use the same outer-option field types and start non-required properties absent. Apply this mode throughout generated object fields, including enum payloads and referenced or combined schemas; required fields and flattened additional-prope
